long_biography.plain_text:
Dutch developer Jo Roelof Zeeman created his own housing-guarantee foundation to protect buyers if a contractor failed. Its work included visiting every Zeeman Vastgoed project. He recruited experienced public administrators and construction specialists to its board, including people whose scrutiny he believed could strengthen the business.

In his private property fund, he sought smaller, well-let buildings in locations with scope to increase in value. He spread investments across shops, offices, homes and industrial premises, and judged purchase prices against rental income. After selling his listed-company stake, he kept the new vehicle private. Purchases were partly financed through longstanding relationships with Rabobank and ING.
